lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Skills and Flexible Meal Planning
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: storage and cleanup

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic storage and cleanup task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: After a real meal or snack is prepared or eaten in their household, the learner stores any real leftover or perishable food using correct timing and storage practice, then completes a full cleanup of the actual prep area used, comparing this attempt to how they have handled storage and cleanup before.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real meal, leftovers, or used prep area are available at the time of this lesson, the learner instead works through a provided list of five food-storage and cleanup scenarios, identifying what is wrong with each and what the correct action would have been.

materials: adult-or-local: real leftover or perishable food from an actual meal or snack, if available
adult-or-local: storage containers already in the household
adult-or-local: the real prep area used for that meal or snack
adult-or-local: cleaning supplies already in the household

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain whether you actually corrected the specific habit you named at the start, and describe one concrete change you will make the next time you finish a meal or snack in your household.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Storage practice: Real leftover or perishable food is stored promptly in a suitable container, with timing and container choice reported accurately. | Cleanup completeness: Every real surface, dish, and utensil used is cleaned and listed specifically. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner track real storage and cleanup after one additional meal or snack later in the week and compare whether the corrected habit held up without this lesson prompting it.

resources.title: storage and cleanup worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: After a real meal or snack is prepared or eaten in their household, the learner stores any real leftover or perishable food using correct timing and storage practice, then completes a full cleanup of the actual prep area used, comparing this attempt to how they have handled storage and cleanup before.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact storage and cleanup decision or action.
Model move 2: Before storing or cleaning anything, recall what you were taught earlier in this unit about safe storage timing.
Model move 3: Store any real leftover or perishable food from your meal or snack, checking timing and container choice.

Model check: Storage practice: Real leftover or perishable food is stored promptly in a suitable container, with timing and container choice reported accurately. | Cleanup completeness: Every real surface, dish, and utensil used is cleaned and listed specifically.

resources.title: storage and cleanup action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for storage and cleanup.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: storage and cleanup coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: After a real meal or snack is prepared or eaten in their household, the learner stores any real leftover or perishable food using correct timing and storage practice, then completes a full cleanup of the actual prep area used, comparing this attempt to how they have handled storage and cleanup before.
Coach direction: Before storing or cleaning anything, recall what you were taught earlier in this unit about safe storage timing.
Learner prompt: Name one specific storage habit from earlier in this unit that you have not consistently followed, and why.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: storage and cleanup complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Store any real leftover or perishable food from your meal or snack, checking timing and container choice.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I moved perishable leftovers into storage within a reasonable time after the meal or snack ended, rather than leaving them out.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I used a container that actually seals or covers the food, and labeled or noted the date if the household does this.

Equal-access rule: If no real meal, leftovers, or used prep area are available at the time of this lesson, the learner instead works through a provided list of five food-storage and cleanup scenarios, identifying what is wrong with each and what the correct action would have been.

resources.title: storage and cleanup minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain whether you actually corrected the specific habit you named at the start, and describe one concrete change you will make the next time you finish a meal or snack in your household.

Success checks: Storage practice: Real leftover or perishable food is stored promptly in a suitable container, with timing and container choice reported accurately. | Cleanup completeness: Every real surface, dish, and utensil used is cleaned and listed specifically.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: storage and cleanup supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional storage and cleanup condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Storage practice: Real leftover or perishable food is stored promptly in a suitable container, with timing and container choice reported accurately. | Cleanup completeness: Every real surface, dish, and utensil used is cleaned and listed specifically..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
